teaser.text: Anglo American plc is a mining company: it digs up materials that other businesses turn into power equipment, steel, jewellery and fertilizer. To understand how a dollar comes in and goes out, follow three linked questions: what is sold, what it costs to make and deliver, and who buys it.

stock.title: Anglo stock forecast
stock.meta_description: Anglo's forecast weighs production recovery, Teck benefits, cash conversion, free cash flow and valuation.
stock.opening: Anglo's weighted price is 2,552.12 GBp in October 2027 and 3,953.73 GBp in October 2029, with 32% bear, 48% base and 20% bull probabilities. It hinges on production recovery.
stock.closing: The full memo also explains Anglo's business, its rivals, its management and its risks.

paragraphs.text: The first forecast point is October 2027. Its weighted price is 2,552.12 GBp, implying a 37% loss including dividends. The last point is October 2029. Its weighted price is 3,953.73 GBp, still a 1% loss. The bear case has 32% probability, the base case 48% and the bull case 20%.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for Anglo's forecast?

paragraphs.text: EBITDA is the main operating driver. The base path rises from $9,700m to $13,000m because the H1 2026 underlying EBITDA run rate was $8,004m, copper prices strengthened, and 2027 production guidance rises to 750–810kt of copper and 59–63Mt of premium iron ore. Teck contributes progressively, while synergies build toward the targeted $800m annually.

The bear path reaches only $9,000m because weaker prices, lower Chilean grades and delayed recovery reduce Anglo’s core earnings; Teck contributes less and integration costs persist. The bull path reaches $15,500m because stronger copper, improved grades, production at or above guidance and successful integration compound. Q2 copper production was flat, while Collahuasi and Quellaveco faced grade pressure.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Anglo really make?

paragraphs.text: Anglo’s own free-cash-flow measure was $790 million, while the calculation here reaches $1,257 million. A further measure deducts stock pay as an economic cost, producing “real free cash flow” of $1,128 million.
The useful conclusion is not that one definition is correct, but that cash must be tested against maintenance, project timing and repeatability before it is treated as durable surplus.

dividend.title: Anglo dividend: payout and cash cover
dividend.meta_description: Anglo's dividend history, cash coverage, payout outlook and yield against its share price, in plain English.
dividend.opening: Anglo's base dividends rise from $0.40 to $0.76 as earnings recover under the 40% payout policy. In 2025, free cash flow of $1,257 million exceeded shareholder payments of $446 million, though the improvement partly reflected paying less out.
dividend.closing: The full memo also examines Anglo's business, its rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: How much does Anglo pay in dividends per share?

paragraphs.text: Base dividends rise from $0.40 to $0.76 as earnings recover under the 40% payout policy. The first figure is close to the latest ordinary annual run rate, while later payments remain below the implied policy maximum because capital needs continue. The bear path falls from $0.23 to zero as earnings weaken; the bull rises to $1.20 as copper, production and Teck benefits improve cash earnings. The special dividend is excluded.

blocks.heading: Is Anglo's dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: Shareholder payments fell sharply. They were US$5,131 million in 2021. By 2025 they were US$446 million. Free cash flow, the cash left after the operating and investment spending included in the measure, was US$348 million in 2024 and US$1,257 million in 2025. The improvement partly reflected paying less out, not only better mine performance.

Anglo’s own free-cash-flow measure was $790 million, while the calculation here reaches $1,257 million. A further measure deducts stock pay as an economic cost, producing “real free cash flow” of $1,128 million.

paragraphs.text: Management guides to 700–760 kt of copper and 55–59 Mt of premium iron ore in 2026. The 2027 ranges are 750–810 kt and 59–63 Mt. Copper unit-cost guidance is 145 cents per pound in 2026. Premium iron ore guidance is $41 per tonne. Continuing-operations capital expenditure is $3.2 billion in 2026, alongside a 40% dividend payout ratio.

During 2027–2029, evidence of production at guidance, the targeted synergies, dependable water and free-cash-flow conversion above the H1 anchor would move the forecast upward. Persistent Woodsmith spending, integration costs or weak cash conversion would move it downward.
